statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-88822 ("QUIC Uses Uninitialized Stack Bytes During Automated Peer Detection", Low) affects OpenSSL 3.5 and is fixed on the openssl-3.5 branch for OpenSSL 3.5.10, which is not released yet: https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20261110.txt, fix https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/1a73dc590cbad62d6f0329ea4779eadaa8d8fd75, which initialises the address buffer that BIO_dgram_detect_peer_addr() fills from getpeername() and passes its full size as the length. The published DHI Alpine 3.23 openssl builds are 3.5.4-r0, 3.5.5-r0, 3.5.5_git20260330-r1, 3.5.6-r0, 3.5.6-r1, 3.5.7-r0, 3.5.7-r1, 3.5.8-r0, 3.5.8-r1, 3.5.9-r0, 3.5.9-r1 and 3.5.9-r2; we checked the libcrypto3 and libssl3 packages of each on x86_64 and aarch64 against the debug symbols in the openssl-dbg package of the same build, matched by build ID, each package verified against the index checksum. 3.5.9-r2 is OpenSSL 3.5.9 rebuilt with that commit applied: on x86_64 and aarch64 its libcrypto.so.3 has a larger dgram_ctrl(), the function the commit changes, than 3.5.9-r0 and 3.5.9-r1 have (1882 against 1860 bytes on x86_64, 1796 against 1772 on aarch64). Every build from 3.5.5-r0 to 3.5.9-r1 has the same unfixed dgram_ctrl() size as 3.5.9-r0 on both architectures, and 3.5.4-r0 is OpenSSL 3.5.4. Alpine lists the fix in its own 3.5.9-r1: https://security.alpinelinux.org/vuln/CVE-2026-88822 and https://secdb.alpinelinux.org/v3.23/main.json, but the DHI Alpine 3.23 build numbered 3.5.9-r1 does not carry it, so 3.5.9-r2 is the first fixed DHI build. The openssl-fips packages built from the same source hold the FIPS provider fips.so, whose debug symbols in openssl-dbg have no dgram_ctrl() in any build.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-88822 ("QUIC Uses Uninitialized Stack Bytes During Automated Peer Detection", Low) affects OpenSSL 3.5 and is fixed on the openssl-3.5 branch for OpenSSL 3.5.10, which is not released yet: https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20261110.txt, fix https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/1a73dc590cbad62d6f0329ea4779eadaa8d8fd75, which initialises the address buffer that BIO_dgram_detect_peer_addr() fills from getpeername() and passes its full size as the length. Debian lists trixie as vulnerable with no fixed version: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-88822. DHI backports that commit into its standard Debian 13 openssl builds, starting with the second DHI build of 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 and in every later standard build: the third and fourth DHI builds of 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 and both DHI builds of 3.5.9-1~deb13u1. On amd64 and arm64 those builds' libssl3t64 has a dgram_ctrl() that passes the full 112-byte address size to getpeername() when detecting the peer address, where the unfixed code passes 16, which is the length change the commit makes (read from the disassembly, with the function located through the libssl3t64-dbgsym debug symbols matched by build ID); we checked the libssl3t64 package of every published Debian 13 openssl build on both architectures, each verified against the index SHA256. Their changelogs also carry the backport entry. Every earlier standard build has the unfixed 16-byte length in dgram_ctrl() and no changelog entry for this CVE: Debian has not shipped the fix, and DHI added the backport with the second 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 build. The FIPS builds of openssl (the +fips versions in the DHI security repository) are affected: the FIPS build is pinned to the validated upstream release and does not take this backport. Every FIPS build's libssl3t64 has the unfixed 16-byte length in dgram_ctrl() on both architectures, and their changelogs have no entry for this CVE. The advisory's "FIPS impact: no" covers the FIPS provider module only; the affected code is in libcrypto, which the FIPS builds ship without the fix. The FIPS provider fips.so in every published openssl-provider-fips package has no dgram_ctrl(), read from its openssl-provider-fips-dbgsym debug symbols matched by build ID. A FIPS build sorts above the standard builds of the same Debian version, so the range has three affected spans: every build below the first fixed 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 build, the 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 FIPS build up to the first 3.5.9-1~deb13u1 build, and the 3.5.9-1~deb13u1 FIPS build onward.
